chunks: Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad, from Jaʿfar ibn Muḥammad ibn Abī Zayd, said:
Al-Riḍā عليه السلام was asked about the skins of properly slaughtered foxes. He said: “Do not perform salat (prayer) in them.”

key_terms.الثَّعَالِبِ: foxes, the specific animal mentioned in the ruling
key_terms.الذَّكِيَّةِ: properly slaughtered according to religious law
key_terms.الرِّضَا: Imam al-Riḍā عليه السلام, the Imam being asked for the ruling
key_terms.جُلُودِ: skins or hides used as clothing material
key_terms.فِيهَا: in them, meaning in those skins

ai.seo_question: Is it permissible to perform salat (prayer) wearing properly slaughtered fox skins according to Imam al-Riḍā عليه السلام?
ai.summary: This hadith conveys a legal ruling from Imam al-Riḍā عليه السلام concerning salat (prayer) in garments made from fox skins, even when the animal has been properly slaughtered. It indicates the impermissibility of performing salat (prayer) in such skins and is relevant to rulings on clothing used in worship.
